gaps.sentence: Look at the time! We ___ discussing one agenda item for an hour.
gaps.explanation: 'For an hour' and still relevant — present perfect continuous.

gaps.sentence: She ___ to the gym three times a week, mostly before work.
gaps.hint: three times a week shows a routine
gaps.explanation: Frequency expressions like 'three times a week' describe habits, which take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: When I got home, I realised I ___ my keys at the office.
gaps.explanation: 'Had left' — the leaving happened before the realising.

gaps.sentence: When I came downstairs, the whole house ___ of fresh bread.
gaps.hint: smell as a state verb in past
gaps.explanation: 'Smell' as a state verb takes simple tenses, here the past simple: smelled.

gaps.sentence: I ___ her at a conference in 2019, but we did not start working together until last year.
gaps.hint: in 2019 pins a finished past time
gaps.explanation: 'In 2019' is a finished past time, so the past simple is required: met.

gaps.sentence: The train ___ faster than the bus, so we always take the train.
gaps.explanation: Timeless comparisons take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: The taxi ___ as soon as you come out of the terminal — look for a blue shirt.
gaps.hint: in progress at the future arrival moment
gaps.explanation: An action that will be in progress at a future moment takes the future continuous: will be waiting.

gaps.sentence: When she ___ the invoice tomorrow, please pay it immediately.
gaps.explanation: After time conjunctions like 'when' referring to the future, use the present simple.
